threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus doesn’t stop at the curb and the driver just waves you on. We’ve all been there.
Caught a late-night bus and saw a guy offering free hugs near the market. He was surprisingly popular, must've given out at least thirty before it hit midnight.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy on the corner selling homemade falafel from a bicycle at 2 AM, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a late-night döner kebab while listening to street performers rap in German, blending cultures right on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local when they don’t flinch at the smell of sourdough but wrinkle their nose at the whiff of a freshly opened kombucha.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Civic Center bus stuck behind a yoga class blocking the intersection. Only in SF do we need to navigate traffic around downward dogs.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always miss that Gràcia’s plazas are vibrant at dusk. They flock to the touristy spots while we enjoy spontaneous concerts and local chatter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by how they struggle with the 'x' in 'coca de llardons'—the locals roll it off the tongue like it's second nature.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the Overground’ instead of ‘the G’, and you have no clue about secret bus routes. Good luck figuring out the night tube schedule!
Last night on the 59, saw a guy in a full tuxedo serenading a group of drunk friends. Only in Brixton would you find an impromptu opera on a night bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a mom juggling a toddler, a dog, and a grocery bag while chatting on her phone, all without breaking a sweat. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg's street vendors sell currywurst at 3 AM, while other cities are closing up shop? It's a late-night salvation.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission if they can name at least five taco trucks that aren’t on food apps but still serve fire burritos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The other day, a saxophonist serenaded a bus full of commuters stuck at the Civic Center. Only in SF do the delays come with a soundtrack.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love to grab their ‘totally local’ coffee in Gràcia, but most don’t realize it’s the locals who prefer the hidden corner bars over the trendy spots.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily; they’re the ones still trying to pronounce 'Eixample' correctly while juggling a map and a gelato.
